newsitem.title: CANADA: AEC to post C$179 mln Q2 gain.
newsitem.headline: AEC to post C$179 mln Q2 gain.

text.p: Alberta Energy Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it expected to post a second-quarter gain of C$161 million or $1.61 a share from the reorganization of its pipeline division.
The units of AEC Pipelines, which were offered to the public in a C$1.1 billion limited partnership, began trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
AEC retained 70 percent of the limited partnerhip units and received about C$300 million in proceeds from the offering.
Meanwhile, AEC said big jumps in oil and natural gas prices and production volumes led to record first-quarter cash flow.
Cash flow in the period rose to C$165 million or C$1.41 a share, a 64 percent increase from C$101 million or C$1 a share last year.
The company said gas sales in the first quarter averaged 645 million cubic feet per day, up 20 percent from last year.
Crude oil and gas liquids production was 56,000 barrels a day, a 10 percent increase from the first quarter of 1996.
Of total liquids output, conventional production rose 23 percent to 29,417 barrels a day and synthetic production from its stake in Syncrude Canada Ltd decreased slightly to 26,583 barrels a day.
Prices for conventional oil averaged C$24.69 a barrel in the first quarter, up 23 percent, while synthetic crude fetched C$30.13 a barrel, up 29 percent, AEC said.
The company's average gas price was C$2.10 per million British thermal units, a jump from C$1.75 in the first quarter of 1996.

It said drilling activity included 71 exploration wells and 120 development wells with an overall sucess rate of 83 percent. Of the 191 wells, 191 were oil, 23 were gas and 23 were cased for further evaluation, the company said.
AEC's C$600 million 1997 drilling program, which includes 250 exploration and 200 development wells was on target, the company said.
